<!-- en -->
v0.1.11 unifies and then splits the mimocode client identity — every session from the shared MiMo database is now attributed to `MiMo Code` (CLI) or `MiMo Desktop` automatically, with a lossless, rollback-safe database migration. It also makes dimension grouping case-insensitive across every view and stops oversized JSONL lines from failing whole collection files.

### Changed
- The mimocode client is split into `MiMo Code` and `MiMo Desktop`. The `mimocode` config key is unchanged and still covers the one shared local database (`~/.local/share/mimocode/mimocode.db`); the config TUI still lists only the key. Attribution is decided per session from the database's `session.version` marker: a session strictly matching `desktop-<hex-hash>` belongs to `MiMo Desktop`, and every other form — `0.x` CLI versions, the `2.1.x` series, empty or unseen shapes — belongs to `MiMo Code`; provider and model never influence the decision. `query`, sessions, the dashboard, charts, and CSV exports now show both clients as separate rows.
- Existing data migrates automatically. Two schema migrations run on first open of `usage.db` (for example when the daemon starts or a database-backed query or collection command runs). v4 folds the legacy stored name `Xiaomi MiMo / MiMo Code` into `MiMo Code` — same-id rows merge deterministically, no primary-key errors, no duplicated messages or double-counted tokens, single transaction, retried on the next open if it fails. v5 schedules an automatic, resumable reconciliation for the next mimocode collection (including daemon startup catch-up) that re-keys existing rows by the attribution rules: batches run in single transactions (merge opposite-client history → apply current source values → delete merged rows → advance progress), history is preserved losslessly (messages already deleted from the source database are re-keyed, not lost; sessions that no longer exist in the source keep their stored identity). Later mimocode collections also re-key a touched session in the same write transaction if its version now maps to the other client, so a version change cannot leave the same message under both clients or double-count tokens. A database-backed query can install the migrations but does not read the MiMo source database, so the initial split finishes on the next mimocode collection. No special migration command is required; `collect all --client mimocode` explicitly re-arms and reruns the complete assignment reconciliation, including sessions whose source messages have already been removed.
- Rollback to v0.1.10 stays safe. Database triggers keep protecting the data after a self-update rollback: a legacy-name write from an old binary is rewritten to `MiMo Code` and then to `MiMo Desktop` when the session is already known to be Desktop — same id, single row, no double counting — and any such write re-arms the reconciliation marker so the next mimocode collection self-heals sessions that were new during the rollback window.
- Dimension grouping is case-insensitive in every view. Values that differ only by case — for example `GLM-5.3-Flash` and `glm-5.3-flash` — merge into a single row showing the spelling with the most requests, in the built-in views, custom views, heatmaps, the dashboard, and exported data alike. Provider aliases now also match case-insensitively (exact matches still win), and the active-clients count in `query summary` folds case variants the same way.

### Fixed
- Oversized JSONL lines no longer fail whole files. Codex session-compaction events can write multi-megabyte single lines (17 MiB and beyond observed); with the previous 16 MiB per-line cap such a line aborted the entire file's collection with a partial-read error. The cap is raised to 32 MiB and lines beyond it are now skipped individually — the rest of the file still collects. After updating, restart the daemon so its startup catch-up re-reads existing JSONL files. If the error came from a manual collection, rerun the same date/range or use `token-usage collect retry --client codex`; a bare `token-usage collect` only collects today.

### Installation
See the [README Quick Start](https://github.com/YuLaiZ/token-usage#quick-start). Existing users update in place with `token-usage update`.

<!-- zh -->
v0.1.11 将 mimocode 客户端身份统一后拆分——共用 MiMo 数据库中的每个会话自动归属 `MiMo Code`（CLI）或 `MiMo Desktop`，数据库迁移自动、无损且可承受回滚。本版同时让所有视图的维度分组不再区分大小写，并修复超长 JSONL 行导致整文件采集失败的问题。

### 变更
- mimocode 客户端拆分为 `MiMo Code` 与 `MiMo Desktop`。配置键 `mimocode` 保持不变、仍覆盖同一本地数据库（`~/.local/share/mimocode/mimocode.db`），配置 TUI 也仍只显示配置键。归属按数据库 `session.version` 标记逐会话判定：严格匹配 `desktop-<十六进制hash>` 归 `MiMo Desktop`，其余一切形态——`0.x` CLI 版本、`2.1.x` 序列、空值与未见过的形态——归 `MiMo Code`；provider/model 永不影响判定。`query`、会话明细、仪表板、图表与 CSV 导出将以两行分别呈现。
- 存量数据自动迁移。新版本第一次打开 `usage.db` 时（例如 daemon 启动，或运行会访问数据库的查询、采集命令时）执行两个 schema 迁移：v4 把旧落库名 `Xiaomi MiMo / MiMo Code` 折叠为 `MiMo Code`（同 id 行确定性合并，不报主键冲突、不产生重复消息或 token 双计；单事务，失败下次打开重试）；v5 为下一次 mimocode 采集（包括 daemon 启动补采）调度自动、可恢复的 reconciliation，按归属规则重归属存量行——分批单事务（合并另一侧历史行 → 应用当前源值 → 删除已合并行 → 推进进度），历史无损（源库已删除的消息被重归属而非丢失，源库中已消失的会话保持库内身份不动）。后续 mimocode 采集若发现本轮触达的会话 version 已改判另一 client，会在同一写事务中迁移该会话历史，避免同一消息落在两侧或 token 双计。数据库查询可以安装迁移，但不会读取 MiMo 源库，因此首次拆分会在下一次 mimocode 采集时完成。无需专门的迁移命令；`collect all --client mimocode` 会显式重新置位并完整重跑 assignments reconciliation，连源消息已删除但 session 仍存在的历史行也会复核。
- 回滚到 v0.1.10 仍然安全。自更新回滚后数据库 trigger 持续保护数据：旧版二进制写入的旧长名被改写为 `MiMo Code`，会话已知属 Desktop 时再改写为 `MiMo Desktop`——同 id 单行、不双计；且任何此类写入都会重置 reconciliation 标记，下一次 mimocode 采集会自动修正回滚期间新出现的会话。
- 所有视图的维度分组不再区分大小写。仅大小写不同的值——例如 `GLM-5.3-Flash` 与 `glm-5.3-flash`——合并为一行，行内显示请求数最多的拼写；内置视图、自定义视图、热力图、仪表板与导出数据一致生效。provider 别名同样改为大小写不敏感匹配（精确匹配仍优先），`query summary` 的活跃客户端数按同一口径折叠计数。

### 修复
- 超长 JSONL 行不再导致整文件失败。Codex 会话压缩事件会写出数 MiB 的单行（实测有 17 MiB 以上）；此前 16 MiB 的单行上限会让整份文件采集以 partial read 错误中止。上限提升到 32 MiB，超限行改为单独跳过——文件其余部分照常采集。升级并重启 daemon 后，启动补采会重新读取现有 JSONL 文件。若错误来自手工采集，请重新执行原日期/范围，或运行 `token-usage collect retry --client codex`；裸 `token-usage collect` 默认只采今天。

### 安装
见 [README 快速开始](https://github.com/YuLaiZ/token-usage/blob/main/README.zh-CN.md#快速开始)。已有用户用 `token-usage update` 原地升级。
